parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define the term standard cell potential.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Draw a fully labelled diagram of the experimental set-up you could use to measure the standard electrode potential of the $\text{Pb}^{2+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Pb(s)}$ electrode. Include the necessary chemicals.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text:
The $E^{\ominus}$ for a $\text{Pb}^{2+}\text{(aq)}/\text{Pb(s)}$ electrode is $-0.13\text{ V}$.

Suggest how the $E$ for this electrode would differ from its $E^{\ominus}$ value if the concentration of $\text{Pb}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ ions is reduced. Indicate this by placing a tick (✓) in the appropriate box in the table.

| more negative | no change | less negative |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
|  |  |  |

Explain your answer.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem:
Car batteries are made up of rechargeable lead-acid cells. Each cell consists of a negative electrode made of $\text{Pb}$ metal and a positive electrode made of $\text{PbO}_2$. The electrolyte is $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\text{(aq)}$.

When a lead-acid cell is in use, $\text{Pb}^{2+}$ ions are precipitated out as $\text{PbSO}_4\text{(s)}$ at the negative electrode.

$$\text{Pb(s)} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}\text{(aq)} \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4\text{(s)} + 2\text{e}^-$$

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: Calculate the mass of $\text{Pb}$ that is converted to $\text{PbSO}_4$ when a current of $0.40\text{ A}$ is delivered by the cell for $80$ minutes.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Complete the half-equation for the reaction taking place at the positive electrode.

$$\text{PbO}_2\text{(s)} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}\text{(aq)} + \ldots\ldots + \ldots\ldots \rightarrow \text{PbSO}_4\text{(s)} + \ldots\ldots$$

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The diagrams show how the voltage across two different cells changes with time when each cell is used to provide an electric current.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

Suggest a reason why

- the voltage of the lead-acid cell changes after several hours,

- the voltage of the fuel cell remains constant.
